judges.9.p1.b1.text: “Please ask all the leaders of Shechem, ‘Is it better for you that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or just one man?’ Remember that I am your own flesh and blood.”

judges.9.p1.b3.text: So they gave him seventy shekels of silver from the temple of Baal-berith, with which Abimelech hired some worthless and reckless men to follow him.

judges.9.p2.b4.text: He went to his father’s house in Ophrah, and on one stone murdered his seventy brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal.

judges.9.p2.b5.text: But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, survived, because he hid himself.

judges.9.p2.b6.text: Then all the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo gathered beside the oak at the pillar in Shechem and proceeded to make Abimelech their king.

judges.9.p3.b7.text: When this was reported to Jotham, he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim, raised his voice, and cried out:

judges.9.p3.b8.text: Listen to me, O leaders of Shechem, and may God listen to you.

judges.9.p4.b9.text: One day the trees set out to anoint a king for themselves. They said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’

judges.9.p4.b10.text: Should I stop giving my oil that honors both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?

judges.9.p4.b11.text: Should I stop giving my wine that cheers both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?

judges.9.p4.b12.text: If you really are anointing me as king over you, come and find refuge in my shade. But if not, may fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon.

judges.9.p5.b13.text: for my father fought for you and risked his life to deliver you from the hand of Midian, but you have risen up against my father’s house this day and killed his seventy sons on a single stone, …

judges.9.p5.b14.text: But if not, may fire come from Abimelech and consume the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo, and may fire come from the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo and consume Abimelech.

judges.9.p5.b15.text: Then Jotham ran away, escaping to Beer, and he lived there for fear of his brother Abimelech.

judges.9.p6.b16.text: After Abimelech had reigned over Israel for three years,

judges.9.p6.b17.text: God sent a spirit of animosity between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem and caused them to treat Abimelech deceitfully,

judges.9.p6.b18.text: The leaders of Shechem set up an ambush against Abimelech on the hilltops, and they robbed all who passed by them on the road.

judges.9.p6.b19.text: So this was reported to Abimelech.

judges.9.p7.b20.text: Meanwhile, Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers and crossed into Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem put their confidence in him.

judges.9.p7.b21.text: And after they had gone out into the fields, gathered grapes from their vineyards, and trodden them, they held a festival and went into the house of their god; and as they ate and drank, they cursed Abimelech.

judges.9.p7.b22.text: Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? … If only this people were under my authority, I would remove Abimelech; …

judges.9.p7.b23.text: Muster your army and come out!

judges.9.p8.b24.text: Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you. Now then, tonight you and the people with you are to come and lie in wait in the fields.

judges.9.p8.b25.text: So Abimelech and all his troops set out by night and lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.

judges.9.p8.b26.text: Look, people are coming down from the mountains!

judges.9.p8.b27.text: The shadows of the mountains look like men to you.

judges.9.p9.b28.text: Look, people are coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming by way of the Diviners’ Oak.

judges.9.p9.b29.text: Where is your gloating now? … You said, ‘Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?’ … Go out now and fight them!

judges.9.p9.b30.text: So Gaal went out before the leaders of Shechem and fought against Abimelech, but Abimelech pursued him, and Gaal fled before him. And many Shechemites fell wounded all the way to the entrance of the gate.

judges.9.p9.b31.text: Abimelech stayed in Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.

judges.9.p10.b32.text: The next day the people of Shechem went out into the fields, and this was reported to Abimelech. So he took his men, divided them into three companies, and lay in wait in the fields. …

judges.9.p10.b33.text: Then Abimelech and the companies with him rushed forward and took their stand at the entrance of the city gate. The other two companies rushed against all who were in the fields and struck them down.

judges.9.p10.b34.text: And all that day Abimelech fought against the city until he had captured it … Then he demolished the city and sowed it with salt.

judges.9.p11.b35.text: On hearing of this, all the leaders in the tower of Shechem entered the inner chamber of the temple of El-berith.

judges.9.p11.b36.text: he and all his men went up to Mount Zalmon. Abimelech took his axe in his hand and cut a branch from the trees, which he lifted to his shoulder, …

judges.9.p11.b37.text: Hurry and do what you have seen me do.

judges.9.p11.b38.text: So each man also cut his own branch and followed Abimelech. Then they piled the branches against the inner chamber and set it on fire above them, killing everyone in the tower of Shechem, about a thousand men and women.

judges.9.p12.b39.text: Then Abimelech went to Thebez, … and captured it. But there was a strong tower inside the city, and all the men, women, and leaders of the city fled there. They locked themselves in and went up to the roof of the tower.

judges.9.p12.b40.text: When Abimelech came to attack the tower, he approached its entrance to set it on fire.

judges.9.p12.b41.text: But a woman dropped an upper millstone on Abimelech’s head, crushing his skull.

judges.9.p12.b42.text: Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, ‘A woman killed him.’

judges.9.p13.b43.text: And when the Israelites saw that Abimelech was dead, they all went home.

judges.9.p13.b44.text: In this way God repaid the wickedness that Abimelech had done to his father in murdering his seventy brothers.

judges.9.p13.b45.text: And God also brought all the wickedness of the men of Shechem back upon their own heads. So the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.
